title: A Reply from Tyvaren
location: Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Secure Communications Room

narrative.text: The reply from Tyvaren arrives via diplomatic courier — an actual courier, a young woman in a Tyvaren military uniform who hands the envelope to Vyktor personally and waits for a response. Vukov has replied in his own hand. The letter is terse, soldierly, but not dismissive.

Marshal Vukov writes: 'Chancellor. Your letter reached my desk. Soldiers do not write letters — they write orders. But you are not a soldier, and this is not a war. Not yet. I will meet you. One meeting. No staff, no minutes, no press. If you are genuine, we may find a path that does not lead through the Gravenmark Pass. If you are not, it will be the last meeting between our nations before the guns begin.'

He is agreeing to talk. That is more than I expected from Vukov — he is not known for diplomacy. Either your letter was exceptionally well-written, or his generals are less enthusiastic about this war than their public statements suggest. Either way, we have a window. A narrow one.

choices.text: "A meeting. One meeting. That is all I asked for. Dusek, prepare a full intelligence briefing — I need to know everything about Vukov before I sit across from him. Vyktor, send my acceptance. We have a chance to prevent this war. Let us not waste it."
